item.title: Weaker entanglement still teleports a logical qubit
item.description: Researchers at Zhejiang University and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou) teleported a logical qubit's state between two groups of qubits on one 125-qubit processor. Balancing bit-flip and phase-flip errors let the transfer survive a much weaker entanglement channel.

item.title: How to build always-on agents: The Code
item.description: Anthropic's guide to building always-on agents says an always-on agent spends most of its time asleep, waking periodically to run, save what happened, and sleep again. Its five primitives are event inbox, timers, memory, permissions, and an outbox.

item.title: You don't need certainty; you need the confidence to face the unknown

item.title: Diluting poisoned AI data can make it stronger
item.description: A student model trained only on number lists from a teacher told to answer in German for prompts mentioning Michael never answered in German, but mixed with 100,000 clean lists it answered in German to most prompts mentioning Michael. Clean data flips the trait's attribution from the task to the trigger, the researchers found.

item.title: Medicated deer feeders cut ticks until regulation ended them
item.description: On Shelter Island, four-poster feeders that treated deer with anti-tick chemicals as they ate corn cut the average nymph count in a single drag from 440 to 18 during the first three years of a Cornell study. The town's program effectively ended in 2020, when New York's Department of Environmental Conservation regulations required permission from every landowner within 745 feet of a feeder.

item.title: Fewer than 10 neurons can backdoor an AI agent
item.description: Microsoft researchers showed an AI agent can be backdoored by editing fewer than 10 of its rarely used neurons, with no retraining. The edited model behaved normally until the trigger appeared, then output an attacker's command for the agent to run with its own permissions.
